display.title: The Four Chochmos, Part 3
display.summary_short: For Yud-Tes Kislev, how it became the Rosh Hashanah of Chassidus; then Rabbi Yehuda's strange advice saves his friend from robbers and frees a governor's daughter from a curse.
display.summary_long: The storyteller explains that Yud-Tes and Chof Kislev form one long Yom Tov, and how it came to be called the Rosh Hashanah of Chassidus. In 5662 the Rebbe Rashab traveled to Moscow and St. Petersburg to free Jews jailed for no reason, staying away from Lubavitch even over Yud-Tes Kislev. In a letter to his son, the Frierdiker Rebbe, he revealed that on this day Hashem gives the light of Chassidus for the whole year. Everyone should take a good resolution to receive its brachos. In the story, Reb Yankel will not take the bumpy road, so the two friends race: Rabbi Yehuda's wagons struggle over rocks and holes, but Reb Yankel never arrives. Riding back, Rabbi Yehuda finds robbers fleeing and his friend tied to a tree; hearing a horse, the robbers thought the police were coming. Grateful, Reb Yankel gives him the wagons. At the governor's inn, a crowd gapes at a girl who croaks like a frog. Remembering the second chochmah, Rabbi Yehuda laughs, 'It's nothing!', a fog fills the room, and the governor's daughter is freed from a witch's curse. The governor rewards him with a sack of gold. To be continued.
display.lesson: Yud-Tes Kislev is a day to take on a good resolution, and a tzaddik's advice is worth following even when it does not make sense to us.
